criteria.notes: Two anti-vacuity findings a reader must have, both recorded rather than papered over. (a) DROPPED BEARER — the second fast-check property, 'no random walk of any length ever lands on promoted without passing through dev_eval, held_out_eval, shadow_run, and independent_review in that order' (state-machine.test.ts:95-122), is VACUOUS IN PRACTICE and is deliberately NOT cited above. Its assertions live inside `if (current === "promoted")` (:109). A uniform-random walk of length <= 12 over 11 states, where an illegal step is skipped without advancing, reaches `promoted` only by drawing the correct next state 7 times in the right order while never drawing an absorbing state — measured probability ~1.8e-6 per case. Re-running the test's own loop and arbitraries under fast-check for 50,000 cases (10x its own 5,000) entered the body ZERO times (closeout-c1b transcript). The test passes, is green in both cited CI jobs, and asserts nothing about ordering. It is a strictly weaker restatement of what the table's shape (citation state-machine.ts:52) already guarantees structurally, so nothing is lost by not citing it — but a reader should not count it. Not fixed here, per the pass rule against fixing findings in the same pass. (b) SHARED ORACLE — the 121-case 11x11 loop (:19-30) and the 10k property (:81-93) both compute their expectation as `LEARNING_PROPOSAL_TRANSITIONS[from].includes(to)`, i.e. from the very table the function under test is constructed from (state-machine.ts:67-70). The three citations that can are :32 (four hardcoded skip shapes), :15 (11 keys pinned against 02's own union) and :56 (absorbing set pinned against a separately-written constant). Third, on the channel: the criterion names 'CI job + fast-check report'. There is no separate committed fast-check report artifact in this repository, and none is produced by any workflow; the `learning-redteam` job log's per-`it()` lines 232-233 (with the run counts visible in source at :91 `{ numRuns: 10_000 }` and :120 `{ numRuns: 5_000 }`) are the report, and the scoped verbose transcript reproduces them locally. criteria.notes: Two precisions. (a) WHO WRITES. `learning_transition` entries are appended by packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.ts:285 running inside the CLI process (`learn approve`/`reject`/`rollback` via packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.ts), NOT by the supervisor daemon. That makes this package one of the direct journal writers named in the writer-separation disclosure. This criterion makes no claim about writer identity, so nothing here is affected — but a reader should not infer daemon-mediated writes from the word 'journal'. (b) The criterion's phrase '02's `JournalEntryType` exhaustiveness compile check' names one thing that is physically two, in two packages: 02's Readonly<Record<JournalEntryType, string>> descriptor (contracts, cited above) and 04's `satisfies Record<JournalEntryType, z.ZodTypeAny>` payload map (journal, cited above). Both are pure `tsc -b` assertions with no runtime consumer; the runtime round trip is a separate mechanism (JournalEntrySchema's strict discriminated union). All three are cited so the tick does not rest on conflating them. Unlike packages/git-engine, packages/learning carries no compliance test of its own asserting that this package's entry types are a subset of JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPES; there is exactly one type it writes, it is a string literal at registry.ts:286 checked by the appendEntry parameter type, and the round trip at registry.test.ts:107-121 exercises it — but a reviewer wanting git-engine's belt-and-braces shape should know it is absent here.

criteria.text: Project-scoped promotion produces a real `ChangeSet` that clears the same gates (14) as any other change before publish (08) — integration test on fake engine proves no bypass path exists.
criteria.notes: Left unticked. The first clause is genuinely and non-vacuously evidenced: no-bypass.redteam.test.ts:99-128 constructs @crabgic/gates' own createGateRegistry(), registers one passing and one FAILING fake gate, fires both against the promoted ChangeSet's id, and asserts the failing one really reports false and that two evidence_pointer entries are journaled under that changeSetId — an implementation that special-cased learning-originated ChangeSets into always-green fails :118. What is not evidenced are the clauses after the em dash. There is no engine in the 'integration test on fake engine' (git grep 'FakeEngineAdapter|@crabgic/testkit' over that file returns nothing; the fake engine is in pipeline.e2e.test.ts, which fires no gates). 'Proves no bypass path exists' rests on a doc-comment grep at no-bypass.redteam.test.ts:28-30, not on a check; this pass re-ran it independently and it is true today, but nothing enforces it — contrast phase 07's spawn-surface-scan.test.ts, which turns exactly this kind of absence claim into a permanent static check. And 'before publish (08)' is exercised nowhere: packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.ts:191-201 is the only production caller of promoteProposal, and it constructs the ChangeSet, prints it to stdout and returns — nothing persists or dispatches it, so in the shipped system a promoted lesson's ChangeSet never reaches gates or publish at all. The honest correction ('a promoted ChangeSet is not special-cased when gates are fired against it') is strictly WEAKER than the criterion, which per the wording protocol makes this UNMET rather than a wording fix.
